title: Israel to close UK consulate in Jerusalem after sanctions against illegal settlements – UK politics live
text:
Israel to close UK consulate in Jerusalem after sanctions against illegal settlements – UK politics live
Foreign minister, Gideon Saar, claims UK ‘systemically working against the state of Israel’ as MPs including Jeremy Corbyn are also banned from country
US secretary of state Marco Rubio says Washingon won't be following UK and imposing trade ban on Israeli settlements
Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, has been asked about the UK government’s decision to ban trade with illegal Israeli settlements. As Shrai Popat reports on our US live blog, Rubio said that the US was “not going to do what the UK did”. But he did not comment on the decision in detail.
He also said the US does not “want to see some uptick in violence or an uptick in conflict or tensions in the West Bank at a very tenuous time in the region”.
Emma Graham-Harrison is the Guardian’s chief Middle East correspondent
This is from Michael Sfard, one of Israel’s leading human rights lawyers, on the significance of Ed Miliband saying in his statement earlier (see 1.38pm) that the UK government now believes ethnic cleansing is taking place in the West Bank.
Because ethnic cleansing is a mass atrocity that consists of war crimes and might even consist of crimes against humanity, that recognition puts an obligation on the international community, and on the UK that recognises it, to take every legal measure to pressure Israel to stop it.
And that is very important, because that would dictate many aspects of British policy towards Israel.
Greens welcome trade ban for West Bank settlements, but say further action against Israel needed
The Greens have more MPs sanctioned by Israel today (see 4.13pm) than any other party. Here is their response to the settlement trade ban announcement. It is from Ellie Chowns, their parliamentary leader and foreign affairs spokesperson.
The measures announced today mark a critical and overdue step towards upholding the UK’s obligations under international law – one which the Green party has long fought for and strongly supports.
We additionally welcome the government’s recognition that the occupation is unlawful and that Palestinians face ethnic cleansing in the West Bank. Exerting pressure on the Israeli Government over illegal settlements is crucial to protecting the human rights of Palestinians, and Greens are pleased to see action taken to progress this aim.
But Chowns said that the government should have gone further.
Britain’s legal duty to prevent genocide arose when ministers knew, or should have known, of a serious risk. That threshold was crossed long ago. Continuing military and intelligence cooperation with Israel while Palestinians are killed and denied lifesaving aid is a shameful failure to fulfil that duty. Ministers must take further action.
That requires a full two-way arms embargo, wide-ranging sanctions, an end to military and intelligence cooperation, and withdrawal from the UK-Israel trade and partnership agreement.
Existing export licenses that sustain the occupation must be ended, and restrictions must cover F-35 components supplied through the international pool.
Britain must also press for unimpeded humanitarian access and independent war crimes investigations to secure accountability and justice.
Aamna Mohdin is a Guardian community affairs correspondent.
While the leading British Jewish communal organisations have expressed “deep regret” at the government’s decision (see 3.21pm and 4.21pm), the response has not been uniform; progressive Jewish groups have welcomed the announcement.
Yachad, a UK Jewish organisation that advocates for a political resolution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, said:
The UK government’s announcement today that it will ban trade in goods with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, and expand sanctions beyond violent extremists, to include those responsible for deepening and entrenching the occupation, is an important and necessary development. We believe it should be supported by those that support the rights of the seven million Israelis and seven million Palestinians to live with freedom, dignity and security.
These new policies do not target Israel; they target the occupation. They draw a clear distinction between the legitimacy of the state of Israel and the settlement enterprise which is illegal under international law.
Distinguishing settlements from Israel proper is not a judgement on where a border will ultimately fall, it’s a recognition that unilateral facts on the ground should not be allowed to decide that question in advance.
The Board of Deputies of British Jews has released its response to Ed Miliband’s announcement. Here is an excerpt.
As proud Brits who love our country, and who also have a deep religious, cultural and family ties to Israel, we feel a deep sense of anguish about this breakdown in relations. We are also impacted directly by heightened rhetoric about the conflict, including policies that focus on the actions of the Israeli government, and do not sufficiently address responsibilities of Palestinian leaders and malign actors in the region.
Announcing such measures during an already heated Israeli election – which has the potential to lead to considerable change to the situation in the West Bank and Gaza – risks perverse consequences which go against the UK’s stated objectives. We urge both governments to avoid pursuing what appear to be party interests over national interests.
Jeremy Corbyn heads list of 11 British MPs being banned by Israel
Here is the full list of 12 Britons being banned from Israel by the Israeli government following today’s illegal settlements trade ban. Eleven of them are MPs, and the other person, Fahad Ansari, runs an anti-Zionist legal group.
There are five Green MPs on the list, four Labour MPs and two from Your Party.
Saar accuses Miliband of 'outrageous lies' and says UK's trade ban 'morally distorted'
This is what Gideon Saar, the Israeli foreign minister, said as he announced the measures his government is taking in response to the ban on trade with West Bank settlements unveiled in London.
Today, with the agreement of Prime Minister Netanyahu, I decided on a series of Israeli countermeasures in response to the series of new sanctions announced today by the British foreign secretary of the Labour government and following a series of anti-Israel decisions by the Labour government.
The accusations made today by the foreign secretary of the Labour government [Ed Miliband] in the British parliament were outrageous lies.
Let me make this clear from the outset: we have nothing against the British people. We know that we have many friends in Britain.
Unfortunately, a hostile Labour government is in office, systematically acting against the state of Israel, and it has left us with no choice but to finally respond to its hostile actions.
The British move is morally distorted and constitutes blatant interference in the affairs of a sovereign state and in its electoral process.
The attempt by the British Labour government to impose measures in the style of the ‘white paper’ carries echoes of the antisemitic words of British Lieutenant-General Barker, commander of British forces in the Land of Israel during the Mandate, who said: “punish the Jews by striking at their pockets.”
The Jewish people have the right to live throughout the Land of Israel. The connection and right of the Jewish people to this land are documented more extensively than those of any other people in human history.
I say to the Labour government and to every government in the world that thinks it can force Israel to act against our national and security interests: You have no chance of succeeding.
We did not return to our land after 2,000 years only to lose it under pressure from jihadists, Islamists, antisemites, far-leftists and wokes.
Not only will you fail to harm us. You will harm yourselves and your own influence.
The latest decision by the Labour government joins an increasingly escalating series of unilateral measures against Israel adopted by the hostile Labour government since it took office in July 2024.
Miliband's move welcomed by some pro-Palestinian groups - while others say UK should be going much further
Aamna Mohdin
Aamna Mohdin is a Guardian community affairs correspondent.
Ed Miliband’s sweeping sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements, announced alongside France and Canada, have been hailed as a historic step forward by many in the British Palestinian community – though others have urged the Foreign Office to go much further.
Shaher Saed, general secretary of the Palestine General Federation of Trade Unions (PGFTU), said:
We see this as an important step in the right direction and a clear message that the illegal settlement enterprise cannot continue without accountability and consequences. The continued expansion of settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories, accompanied by acts of killing and violence, the burning of property, and the destruction of agricultural land, seriously undermines the prospects for achieving a two-state solution and violates the rights of the Palestinian people.
We encourage the UK government to go further and take stronger and more effective measures to halt settlement expansion, ensure respect for international law, hold those responsible for violations accountable, and protect the rights and livelihoods of Palestinian workers.
The British Palestinian Committee said in a statement:
Today’s announcement by the British foreign secretary indicates a shift in position from the previous Labour administration. It is a necessary and overdue step. Among the announced positions are certain measures which, if implemented and taken further, bring the UK closer to meeting its obligations under international law, and would indicate a shift towards holding Israeli war crimes to account.
Omar Barghouti, co-founder of the BDS movement for Palestinian rights, said:
The announced UK measures against Israel’s settlements are largely performative and ineffective, yet they also reflect the impact of relentless public pressure on the current government. The UK is going after a crime while continuing to be complicit with the serial criminal.
Aside from its shameless, multi-faceted complicity in Israel’s ongoing genocide against the Palestinian people in Gaza, the UK has an unequivocal obligation, arising from the ICJ advisory opinion of July 2024, to end all military, intelligence, trade, academic and other relations with Israel that enable its regime of illegal occupation and apartheid in the occupied Palestinian territory, including East Jerusalem. Insisting on letting ‘humanitarian aid’ into Gaza does not begin to end UK complicity.
Jewish Leadership Council accuses government of having 'increasingly punitive' approach towards Israel
The Jewish Leadership Council, which represents Jewish organisations in Britain, has issued a statement has accused the government of having an “increasingly punitive and unbalanced approach towards Israel”. It also says this risks becoming a “de facto boycott of Israel”.
Palestinian presidency welcomes UK's move, calling it 'important step towards confronting system of Israeli colonial settlement'
The Palestinian presidency has issued a statement welcoming Miliband’s announcement. It describes the move as “an important step toward confronting the system of Israeli colonial settlement and its violations against the Palestinian people”.
In the Commons Andrew Murrison (Con) asked who the government would distinguish between goods made in the Israeli settlements and those made in green line Israel.
Miliband said this would be the responsibility of companies importing good from Israel. He said the sanctions rules would probably use postcodes to identify illegal settlements, and companies importing goods would “have to say that the goods that they are bringing in do not come from those areas”.
Miliband says he may be able to speed up timetable for introduction of ban on trade with illegal settlements
Ed Miliband said in his statement it could take up to nine months to introduce the ban on trade with illegal Israeli settlements. (See 1.50pm.)
The Lib Dems have said the government should act more quickly. Calum Miller, the Lib Dem foreign affairs spokesperson, said:
The settlement trade ban is a long overdue step in the right direction, but ministers now need to move with urgency.
The current extremist Israeli cabinet is racing to establish facts on the ground to prevent a two-state solution. Liberal Democrats are calling on the government to introduce emergency legislation to implement this ban without delay.
In the Commons, when asked if the government would be able to act more quickly, Miliband said this might be possible. He said:
I want to do this as quickly as possible. And I just say this – six to nine months is what I’ve said in the statement, if we can do it quicker, we will.
In the Commons, the first backbench MP to be called to speak was Emily Thornberry, the Labour chair of the foreign affairs committee. She started with the words: “At last.”
Former Israeli PM says UK’s sanctions announcement ‘unavoidable’ result of ethnic cleansing in West Bank
Emma Graham-Harrison
Emma Graham-Harrison is the Guardian’s chief Middle East correspondent
The former Israeli prime minister Ehud Olmert has backed Ed Miliband’s announcement. Olmert told the Guardian:
The British government decision became unavoidable as a result of a continuous effort of ethnic cleansing perpetrated by a large group of Jewish terrorists in the West Bank. The crimes of these terrorists are actively assisted by police and military units over a long period of time. The highest levels of government led by minister of defence Katz and prime minister Netanyahu are actively supporting these terrorists and avoid taking the necessary measures to stop it.
Millions of Israelis are appalled by this terror and are actively resisting the terrorists.
Sanctions are directed against the terrorists not against Israel, and as such they are unavoidable.
Miliband quoted Olmert approvingly in his own statement. (See 1.38pm.)
